newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber mostly up on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber mostly up on shortcovering.

text.p: Rubber futures were largely higher by midday on Monday on mild shortcovering with the market seen looking for direction later this afternoon, dealers said.
"There were some deals done for RSS3 rubber with some traders engaging in a bit of shortcovering. But the rest of the market remained quiet," a local rubber trader said.
Dealers said they were also encouraged by higher Japanese prices. Tokyo and Kobe's benchmark March contract rose 0.8 yen each to reach 135.6 yen in the morning.
"Nothing happened in the ring sessions again. We're hoping for better luck this afternoon," another dealer said.
At around 0445 GMT, November RSS3 was seen at 123.75-125.75 U.S. cents a kg from 123.50 cents.
November RSS1 was indicated at 177.00 Singapore cents (US$1.25) a kg from Friday's settlement of 178.00 cents.
November TSR20 was indicated at 173.00-175.00 Singapore cents (US$1.23-$1.24) a kg against the previous 172.50 cents.
